name: Rio de Janeiro Galeão – Tom Jobim International Airport
before:
Rio's international airport, 20 km north of downtown, and the arrival point for the long haul flights into the city.

Ground transport is better than it looks. The TransCarioca bus rapid transit line runs from both terminals and operates 24 hours a day, with tickets sold at booths on the arrivals level. It links to the metro at Vicente de Carvalho, to suburban rail at several stops, and runs west to Barra da Tijuca and Recreio. A more expensive non-stop service goes to the Gentileza intermodal terminal for the light rail and long distance coaches. There is also a bus to Niterói, and taxis are bookable at company desks in both arrival halls.

Since March 2026 the airport has been jointly managed by RioGaleão, a consortium of Infraero, Changi and Vinci, together with AENA.

The name comes from the beach in front of the original terminal, where the galleon Padre Eterno was built in 1663. Antonio Carlos Jobim was added in 1999, and the airport appears by name in his Samba do Avião.
